5. Verification

View source on GitHubLast updated 3 November 2026

On this page

  2. 5.2 "Not reported" check

For learning only: see the disclaimer in the prompt library index. You stay responsible for every decision.

The output is generated, not retrieved: a fluent answer is produced whether or not it is right. Verification is not optional, and the final check is yours, against the paper. Use these prompts in a new conversation, so the model is not checking its own reasoning in the same context.

5.1 Quote check#

Purpose. Find values whose quotes are not in the paper, or do not support the value.

Prompt
You are verifying a data extraction. Use ONLY the attached paper.

For each row of the table below:
1. Search the paper for the quote. Answer FOUND (verbatim), NEAR (similar wording, give the real text), or NOT FOUND.
2. If FOUND or NEAR: does the passage support the value for the same population, outcome, arm and time period? Answer yes / partly / no, with one sentence.
3. Do not correct values. Only report.

TABLE (study_id,field,value,source_quote,location):
[PASTE CSV ROWS]

Output a CSV with the header: study_id,field,quote_status,supports_value,comment

Check afterwards. Open the paper at every NOT FOUND, NEAR and "partly/no". If you have Python, a mechanical check is more reliable than the model for verbatim matching: python3 .claude/skills/quote-verifier/scripts/verify_quotes.py extraction.csv activity/data/fulltext/ --out verification.csv Failure modes. The model says FOUND for a quote that is not there (it is checking its memory of the paper, not the text). Spot-check a few FOUND rows yourself.

5.2 "Not reported" check#

Purpose. Catch retrieval and parsing failures reported as absence.

Prompt
In the attached paper, look for any information on each of these fields, which were marked "not reported":
[LIST FIELDS WITH THEIR DEFINITIONS]

For each field: search the main text, every table, figure captions and any mention of supplementary material, including synonyms (e.g. healthcare-associated infection, nosocomial, hospital-acquired, infection rate, incidence density).
Answer: PRESENT (quote + location) or ABSENT (list where you looked).

Check afterwards. For each PRESENT, verify the quote. For fields that matter, search the PDF yourself (Ctrl+F) with the synonyms. Failure modes. Information only in figures or supplementary files that the model never received.

5.3 Compare two runs#

Purpose. Check reproducibility of an extraction.

Prompt
Below are two extractions of the same paper made in separate conversations with the same prompt.
Compare them field by field. Output a table: field | run 1 value | run 2 value | same / different / one is more complete.
Do not decide which is right.

RUN 1: [PASTE CSV]
RUN 2: [PASTE CSV]

Check afterwards. Every "different" row goes back to the paper. Outcome numbers are usually less stable than study characteristics. Failure modes. Treating the more detailed run as correct: completeness is not accuracy.
